body.statement: Can the spectral-split adaptive calibration handle produce a rationally outward-rounded moment region that is coordinatewise no wider than the deterministic \(K_\Sigma\)-box with probability tending to one on every interior regular law, while retaining finite-sample coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over the compact class and preserving exact semialgebraic inversion?
body.justification: The fixed worst-case envelope may be conservative, and safe adaptivity is the main route to practically informative global sets.
body.gap: Existing Gaussian covariance bands estimate variance locally, while the required dominance, uniform coverage, rational encoding, and multibranch inversion have not been combined.
body.consumer: The answer determines whether globally honest transfer sets can be narrow enough for routine use without sacrificing validity at branch mergers.
